title: ts-sdk: shape adapters, runtime mappers, and zod/json-schema parity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: teams building with the TypeScript SDK need a predictable, ergonomic way to declare structured output contracts that work both at compile time (type safety) and at runtime (validation) when responses arrive as full payloads or as streaming fragments. Current gaps: (1) hand-rolled runtime validators are inconsistent across examples, (2) streaming fragments break naive Zod validation because partial objects arrive out-of-order, and (3) JSON Schema parity is required for some downstream tools (contract tests, infra wiring).

Goal: deliver a small set of 'shape adapters' + codegen conventions that produce: (a) TypeScript types for structured output, (b) Zod schemas for immediate runtime validation, and (c) JSON Schema artifacts for contract tooling — all generated from a single canonical source (tsdk shape annotations). Also provide streaming-safe runtime mappers that can validate/aggregate partial chunks and emit incremental typed events.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Codegen produces stable TypeScript types + matching Zod schemas for at least three example model outputs (chat-message, search-result, payment-invoice).
- Streaming mapper can accept partial tokens/chunks and produce an incremental 'Partial<T>' state that is Zod-validated on every state transition; final reconciliation validates to the full T or emits a diagnostic when mismatch occurs.
- Generated JSON Schema matches Zod-derived schema for consumer tests (roundtrip check).
- Developer DX: examples in examples/structured-output-playground and README with 3 short snippets (sync generation, streaming mapper usage, and fallback handling).
- Unit tests covering codegen -> runtime mapping and streaming assembly (target 95% coverage for new package).

Non-goals: bundling Zod into minimal runtime yet — we will document tree-shaking and optional peer-dependency patterns instead of forcing a single runtime at this stage.

Design notes and trade-offs considered: 
- Single source of truth: we chose to annotate TypeScript declaration files (tsdoc-style @shape) instead of inventing a new DSL. This keeps DX close to TS authors and leverages existing type information.
- Runtime validator generation: we generate Zod schemas from the annotated types. Alternatives considered: runtime JSON Schema-first approach, but that adds a separate authoring surface.
- Streaming: two approaches considered — (1) validate only at final merge (cheap per-chunk but delayed failure) vs (2) incremental validation per chunk (pessimistic, more CPU). We implement incremental validation but expose a config to throttle validation frequency for high-throughput workloads.
- Bundle size: shipping Zod schemas increases package size. To mitigate we emit a small runtime shim (tsdk-schema-runtime) and make zod a peerDependency; we will provide a prebuilt flavor in a separate package for customers who prefer an all-in-one bundle.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind env TS_SDK_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT; opt-in by updating client config. Start with an internal alpha and Docs-only preview, then invite 2-3 pilot teams (Search, Payments) before wider rollout in ts-sdk-2.4.
comments: 2025-02-06 - Aisha Patel: Initial writeup and spike notes. I prototyped a small generator that maps simple discriminated unions to Zod. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/832 (WIP).

2025-02-10 - Tomás Rivera: Implemented streaming mapper sketch. Key call: createStreamingMapper(schema, options) -> returns {onChunk, snapshot, finalize}. Observed that chunk validation on every token is expensive. Added options.throttleMs for debounce. See branch ts-sdk/feature/streaming-shape-mapper.

2025-02-12 - Linh Nguyen (review): Review feedback - require explicit discriminator field when union members share shapes to avoid ambiguous parsing. Suggest default discriminator name '__type' but allow override via @discriminator annotation. Added unit tests for ambiguous-union case.

2025-02-14 - Security review (internal): Not required for alpha, but remind to document potential DoS vector: maliciously large partial updates causing repeated expensive validations. Mitigation: default maxValidationPerSecond and a circuit-breaker in runtime shim.

2025-02-16 - Tomás Rivera: Merged core codegen for simple shapes and Zod output. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/847. CI failing on two snapshot tests for JSON Schema roundtrip, need to normalize 'additionalProperties' defaults.

2025-02-18 - QA (Maya Singh): Ran manual tests with the Payments pilot dataset. Streaming mapper successfully reconstructed 98% of payloads without diagnostics; failing cases tied to truncated number formats and will be fixed by adding a 'lenientNumber' option during parsing.

2025-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Updated docs and created example playground (internal): https://docs.redwood.com/ts-sdk/structured-output-playground and lightweight demo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/859
